Horror used to be the one genre where ideology took a back seat to scares. The monster was a monster. The killer was a killer. You went, you screamed, you went home. Not anymore.

Over the past decade, horror has become one of Hollywood's preferred vehicles for delivering progressive messaging. Why? Because the genre's built-in tools -- fear, shock, body violation -- map perfectly onto ideological arguments about patriarchy, religious oppression, and systemic injustice. A slasher isn't just a slasher anymore. It's a metaphor. And the metaphor almost always points in the same direction.

Our database contains 102 horror films with complete VirtueVigil Wake Score assessments. Of those, five carry the STRONGLY WOKE verdict, five are WOKE, and ten are WOKE LEAN. Only two managed a MIXED score -- and they barely cleared the threshold. Horror is, by some margin, the most ideologically uniform genre we track. This list ranks the 20 most aggressive examples, from most woke to least, with full scores, verdicts, and links to our complete reviews. Parents: your teenager's next horror pick is probably on this list. Know what's inside it before they press play.

Ranked from most woke to least woke.

#1 (Most Woke): Heretic (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: +27.5 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Streaming • Distributor: A24 • Stars: Hugh Grant, Chloe East, Sophie Thatcher

Heretic is not a horror film that happens to touch on religion. It is a theological assault on Christianity dressed in genre clothing and delivered via Hugh Grant's most charming, murderous performance. Two Mormon missionaries arrive at the home of Mr. Reed, who traps them in his basement and delivers a series of lectures arguing that religion is a con -- an evolutionary "iteration" of ancient control systems. Jesus is equated with Horus and Mithras. Faith is framed as intellectual weakness. Prayer is presented as statistically ineffective. A24 distributed it with pride. Critics gave it 96% on Rotten Tomatoes. Audiences gave it a C+ CinemaScore. That gap tells you everything. At +27.5, Heretic is the most woke horror film in our database of over 700 reviews.

#2: The Bride! (2026)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: +24.4 WOKE

Genre: Gothic Romance / Horror • Platform: Theatrical (IMAX) • Director: Maggie Gyllenhaal • Stars: Jessie Buckley, Christian Bale, Annette Bening

Maggie Gyllenhaal's $80 million reimagining of the Bride of Frankenstein is not subtle. Jessie Buckley's reanimated Bride literally screams "Me too! Me too!" during the climax. She growls "female rage" repeatedly. Women riot in the streets wearing black-ink lip tattoos. Newspapers print "GIRLS RRRIOT." Penelope Cruz's detective assistant gets the badge from her male boss in a "woman vs. patriarchal workforce" arc. The film opened to $8-10 million against its $80 million budget -- a commercial catastrophe. IndieWire called it "a wokified, Joker-fied feminist opera zonked on its own rage." Reason.com called its feminist speeches "nonsense feminist koans." At +24.4, The Bride! is one of the most expensive and explicit ideological statements in horror history.

#3: The Substance (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: +24.1 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Streaming • Director: Coralie Fargeat • Stars: Demi Moore, Margaret Qualley, Dennis Quaid

The Substance is a film about Hollywood's treatment of aging women that uses 21,000 liters of fake blood to make its point. Demi Moore plays Elisabeth Sparkle, an aerobics host fired on her 50th birthday because the network wants someone younger. She injects a black-market serum that splits her into two selves -- her original body and a young, flawless replacement played by Margaret Qualley. The film's thesis is that Hollywood turns women into objects, punishes them for aging, and destroys them when they compete with their own younger selves. Its answer to why this happens is entirely ideological: patriarchy, male gaze, female bodies as products of male consumption. The film received five Oscar nominations, including Best Picture. It is also one of the most graphically extreme films ever to play a multiplex -- extreme body horror, graphic nudity, and a finale involving a grotesque mutant spraying stage blood across a live television audience before exploding. The craft is undeniable. So is the ideology.

#4: Immaculate (2024)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: +21.9 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Theatrical / Hulu • Stars: Sydney Sweeney

Sydney Sweeney spent years developing Immaculate as a vehicle for a message she clearly believed in. The film follows an American nun in an Italian convent who discovers she is pregnant despite being a virgin -- a miracle to the Church, a nightmare to her. Director Michael Mohan confirmed in interviews that the film is a direct abortion allegory. The pregnancy Cecilia carries is one she did not consent to. The institution that impregnated her refuses to acknowledge her autonomy. Her final choice -- to destroy the infant on the convent steps rather than allow it to be born into institutional control -- is presented as liberation and reclaimed agency. This is not subtext. The premise sounds like a devotional horror film. It is an anti-religious, pro-choice horror film instead. At +21.9, Immaculate is one of the most precisely crafted woke traps of the past several years.

#5: Leviticus (2026)

STRONGLY WOKE MARGIN: +19.8 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Romance / Coming-of-Age • Platform: Theatrical / Streaming • Director: Adrian Chiarella

Leviticus is a competent horror film with one very clear ideological mission: to argue that religious communities opposed to homosexuality are not just wrong, but monstrous. The film is named after the biblical book containing the prohibitions on homosexuality that conservative Christians most commonly cite. The setup is familiar coming-of-age territory -- a new kid in a small religious town finds connection and danger -- but the film's argument is that the community's belief system is the source of the horror. A 95% Rotten Tomatoes score tells you everything about the critical establishment's reception. The horror mechanics are well-constructed. The performances are strong. The film's argument -- that Christian communities opposed to homosexuality summon literal evil -- is the entire point.

#6: Clown in a Cornfield (2025)

WOKE MARGIN: +18.6 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Theatrical (RLJE Films / Shudder)

Clown in a Cornfield is a competently made slasher that conceals its political agenda until past the midpoint and then delivers it with zero ambiguity. The first half is efficient genre entertainment: a teenager moves to a small Missouri town, local kids befriend her, someone dressed as the town mascot starts killing. Then the masks come off. The killers are the town's mayor, sheriff, teacher, and shopkeeper -- the entire establishment organizing a murder campaign against the young. The mayor also burned down the town's economic foundation himself. The allegory is direct: the people who claim to restore greatness are the ones who destroyed it. Written during the first Trump term with this allegory explicit and intended, the film's ideology is baked into its structure. Conservative audiences picking this up for genre entertainment deserve to know what they are actually watching.

#7: Midsommar (2019)

WOKE MARGIN: +18.2 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Drama • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Ari Aster • Distributor: A24

Midsommar is a genuinely good film. That is the most important thing to say before everything else, because it shapes how dangerous it is. If Midsommar were a crude feminist horror film, there would be nothing to discuss. It is not crude. Ari Aster's daylight horror follows Dani (Florence Pugh), a woman whose boyfriend Christian is emotionally checked out, as she accompanies him and his friends to a Swedish midsummer festival that turns out to be a pagan cult. The cult systematically dismantles the male characters -- one is seduced and burned alive, another is skinned -- while Dani is embraced, affirmed, and ultimately crowned May Queen. The film frames her journey from grief-stricken girlfriend to cult queen as liberation. The boyfriend is a bad partner, so his horrific death is catharsis. A24 has made a brand out of art-house horror that deconstructs traditional institutions, and Midsommar is their most effective execution: a film that makes you feel good about a woman joining a murder cult because the alternative was a mediocre boyfriend.

#8: MaXXXine (2024)

WOKE MARGIN: +17.9 WOKE

Genre: Horror/Crime • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Ti West • Stars: Mia Goth

Ti West's X trilogy ends the way it began: with a woman who refuses to apologize for wanting more. MaXXXine drops Mia Goth's Maxine Minx into 1985 Los Angeles, where the Night Stalker prowls the streets, the Moral Majority screams from every television, and a former porn star claws her way toward Hollywood legitimacy. The film's ideological framework is unmistakable: the Moral Majority -- representing conservative values and religious objections to the adult film industry -- is positioned alongside a serial killer as one of the threats Maxine must overcome. Her refusal to feel shame about her body, her work, or her ambition is framed as heroic. The film's aesthetic is a love letter to 1980s grindhouse cinema, but its politics are thoroughly contemporary. At +17.9, MaXXXine is a well-made, confidently acted film whose progressive framework is inseparable from its identity.

#9: Presence (2025)

WOKE MARGIN: +14.0 WOKE

Genre: Horror/Thriller • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Steven Soderbergh

Presence is the most technically inventive horror film of early 2025, shot entirely from a ghost's point of view -- the camera drifts through rooms, watches characters from doorways, hovers protectively over the family's neglected daughter Chloe. The formal innovation is genuine and creates real dread. But the ghost is not neutral. It has a worldview, and that worldview is progressive. The Payne family structure is recognizable: an ambitious mother whose career ambition has led to moral compromise, a compliant teenage son being groomed into her worldview, a passive father who cares but cannot act, and a sensitive daughter who sees the family clearly and suffers for it. The presence sides with the daughter in every scene. When a boy catfishes a classmate, the ghost destroys his room. The traditional family as protective institution is the film's villain, and the supernatural force has chosen its side.

#10: Get Out (2017)

WOKE MARGIN: +12.1 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Psychological Thriller • Platform: Theatrical (Universal Pictures / Blumhouse) • Director: Jordan Peele

Get Out is the film that launched Jordan Peele's directing career and won him an Oscar for Best Original Screenplay. It is a very effective horror film built on a very specific political argument: white liberals are the primary threat to Black Americans, they disguise their predation behind progressive language, and the appropriate response is complete distrust of all white relationships. The Armitage family does not burn crosses. They vote for Obama. They say they would have voted a third time if they could. And then they trap Black people in the Sunken Place and auction their bodies to the highest bidder. The film's craft is undeniable -- Daniel Kaluuya's performance is extraordinary, the pacing is relentless, the horror set pieces are earned. But the film's argument that white goodwill is always a mask for predation has been absorbed into the culture so thoroughly that it is now common discourse. For conservative viewers: Get Out is a masterclass in using genre to deliver ideology. It is worth watching for that reason alone -- but know what you are watching.

#11: The First Omen (2024)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +7.4 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Supernatural Thriller • Platform: Theatrical

The 1976 Omen is one of the great supernatural horror films -- a story about a father trying to protect his family from a truth too terrible to accept. The Church figures in it are warnings and helpers. The First Omen is not that film. This prequel reimagines the Catholic Church not as a flawed but real spiritual institution but as a conspiracy of men who engineer the Antichrist's birth through systematic abuse of women's bodies. The nuns are victims. The priests are predators. The Church is the monster. The film's craft is strong and the performances are committed, but the ideological pivot from the original is complete. Where the 1976 film trusted the audience to fear the devil, the 2024 version trusts the audience to fear the institution. At +7.4, The First Omen is a WOKE LEAN that demonstrates how even legacy horror franchises are now being retrofitted with contemporary ideological frameworks.

#12: The Ugly Stepsister (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +6.9 WOKE

Genre: Satirical Black Comedy/Body Horror • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Emilie Blichfeldt

Emilie Blichfeldt looked at Cinderella and asked the question nobody wanted answered: what would the ugly stepsister's story actually feel like if you told it honestly? The answer involves tapeworms, butcher knives, and more blood than a Dario Argento retrospective. The Ugly Stepsister retells the Cinderella story from Elvira's perspective, framing her body modification -- nose jobs, eyelid surgery, tapeworm diets -- as the logical endpoint of beauty standards imposed on women by a patriarchal society. The film is genuinely disturbing and technically accomplished. But its framework -- that women's bodies are sites of social control, that the pursuit of beauty is violence inflicted by men, that Cinderella's "prettiness" is a system of oppression -- is contemporary progressive ideology mapped onto a fairy tale. At +6.9, it's a WOKE LEAN body horror that parents should know about before their teenagers discover it on streaming.

#13: Forbidden Fruits (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +6.6 WOKE

Genre: Comedy Horror • Platform: Theatrical / Shudder

There is a store at the Highland Place mall called Free Eden. It sells cupcake-scented candles, charm bracelets, and overpriced cotton sundresses. The employees are gorgeous. They have their own slang. And at some point after closing time, they gather in a candlelit upper room to perform rituals. Forbidden Fruits is a Shudder-distributed comedy horror that uses its mall-store cult premise to satirize both corporate feminism and millennial consumer culture. The progressive framework is baked into the satire -- the store sells empowerment as a product, and the film knows it. But the satire cuts both ways, which is what keeps it from scoring higher on the woke scale. The tradScore is a relatively strong 21.2, reflecting genuine traditional elements in the narrative's resolution. At +6.6, it's a WOKE LEAN that is more self-aware than most entries on this list.

#14: Ready or Not 2: Here I Come (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +5.7 WOKE

Genre: Horror/Comedy/Thriller • Platform: Theatrical • Stars: Samara Weaving

Ready or Not 2: Here I Come takes the original's eat-the-rich horror-comedy formula and dials it up to a global conspiracy. Samara Weaving returns as Grace, the blood-soaked bride who survived her wealthy in-laws' murderous game night in the 2019 original, and this time the conspiracy extends far beyond one cursed family. The film's ideological framework is the same: the wealthy are literally demonic, their traditions are murderous, and the only moral response is to burn the whole system down while cracking jokes. Whether this is a feature or a bug depends on how you felt about the original. The film's violence-against-the-rich-as-catharsis formula is executed with genuine comic timing and Weaving's committed performance. At +5.7, it is a WOKE LEAN that knows exactly what it is.

#15: The Crow (2024)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +5.5 WOKE

Genre: Action / Horror / Romance • Platform: Theatrical

The original 1994 Crow -- starring Brandon Lee in the role that cost him his life -- is gothic melodrama with no pretensions to realism. It works because Alex Proyas holds Eric's grief and love as the only things that matter. The 2024 remake does not work for the same reason. It tries to update the story for contemporary sensibilities, softening the gothic excess and replacing it with something more self-conscious. The result is a film that loses the original's emotional intensity while adding nothing new. At +5.5, The Crow (2024) is a WOKE LEAN case study in how modern remakes often introduce progressive elements that dilute what made the originals powerful. Conservative viewers who loved the original should approach this remake with low expectations on every front.

#16: Lisa Frankenstein (2024)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +5.0 WOKE

Genre: Horror • Platform: Theatrical (Focus Features) • Writer: Diablo Cody

Lisa Frankenstein is Diablo Cody's Jennifer's Body with worse reviews and a better aesthetic. Set in 1989, it follows a misunderstood teenage girl who resurrects a Victorian-era corpse and falls in love with him while they murder people together. The film is designed to be reclaimed as a feminist cult classic in exactly the way Jennifer's Body was -- a movie misunderstood by critics on release and later celebrated for its subversion of male-gaze horror tropes. Cody writes female desire as inherently transgressive and frames Lisa's murder spree as a darkly comic journey of self-discovery. At +5.0, Lisa Frankenstein is a WOKE LEAN that wears its coming cult-classic status on its sleeve. Parents: the aesthetic is 80s-comedy bright. The content is murder-as-empowerment.

#17: Death of a Unicorn (2025)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +4.6 WOKE

Genre: Dark Fantasy / Comedy Horror • Platform: Theatrical / HBO Max • Stars: Jenna Ortega, Paul Rudd

Let's get the headline out of the way: yes, Death of a Unicorn has a political lean. It is an anti-capitalist satire wrapped in a creature feature, and it does not try to hide it. The rich people are cartoonishly evil. The young progressive woman is the moral compass. The unicorns are nature's revenge on corporate greed. If you have seen Jurassic Park, you know the structure: a wealthy family on a private estate encounters a mythical creature, exploits it for profit, and gets eaten for their trouble. Jenna Ortega and Paul Rudd provide genuine star power and comic timing. At +4.6, Death of a Unicorn is a WOKE LEAN that is more interested in being fun than being a manifesto -- but the manifesto is still there, and parents should know it before handing it to teenagers who might absorb the anti-capitalist framing uncritically.

#18: Us (2019)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +4.2 WOKE

Genre: Horror / Thriller • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Jordan Peele • Stars: Lupita Nyong'o, Winston Duke

Jordan Peele's Us has a problem that Get Out did not: it is trying to do too many things. Get Out was a scalpel. Us is a Swiss Army knife that does not quite close back up properly. The setup is excellent: the Wilson family, headed by Adelaide (Lupita Nyong'o in a genuinely extraordinary dual performance), is terrorized at their beach house by doppelgangers in red jumpsuits carrying golden scissors. The doppelgangers -- the "Tethered" -- are the abandoned underclass, left to rot in underground tunnels while their surface-world copies live comfortable lives. The metaphor is class warfare filtered through horror, and it is ambitious. But the film also wants to be about family, trauma, privilege, and the American dream, and it cannot hold all of them simultaneously. At +4.2, Us is a WOKE LEAN that demonstrates both Peele's extraordinary talent and the limits of using horror as a delivery system for multiple ideological arguments at once.

#19: They Will Kill You (2026)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +4.0 WOKE

Genre: Action/Comedy/Horror • Platform: Warner Bros. Pictures (Theatrical) • Stars: Zazie Beetz

They Will Kill You has exactly one thesis and it commits to it with admirable single-mindedness: put Zazie Beetz in a building full of immortal Satanists and watch what happens. Asia Reaves (Beetz) is an ex-convict who takes a job as a cleaner in a mysterious high-rise in New York, only to discover the building is home to a cult of wealthy Satanists who cannot die. The film is a bloody action-horror-comedy that knows its job is to deliver set pieces, not lectures. But the framework is familiar: the wealthy are literally demonic, the working-class protagonist is our hero, and the violence she inflicts is cathartic justice. At +4.0, They Will Kill You is the mildest WOKE LEAN on this list -- a film whose ideology is present but secondary to its commitment to entertainment.

#20: Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness (2022)

WOKE LEAN MARGIN: +3.4 WOKE

Genre: Action/Adventure/Horror • Platform: Theatrical • Director: Sam Raimi • Stars: Benedict Cumberbatch, Elizabeth Olsen

Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is the MCU's most interesting mess. Sam Raimi brings genuine horror filmmaking to a franchise that desperately needed it, Elizabeth Olsen delivers a villain performance for the ages as the Scarlet Witch, and the multiverse concept finally gets the unhinged treatment it deserves. It is also a film that introduces a teenage character, America Chavez, whose entire narrative function is to be protected by adult heroes while her power -- the ability to punch holes between universes -- serves the plot. The film's progressive credentials are in its casting and representation choices rather than its thesis, which is what keeps it from scoring higher. At +3.4, Doctor Strange in the Multiverse of Madness is the mildest entry on this list -- a WOKE LEAN whose horror credentials come from Raimi's direction rather than its ideology.

What This List Tells Us About Modern Horror

Twenty films. Five STRONGLY WOKE. Five WOKE. Ten WOKE LEAN. Zero TRADITIONAL. Zero TRADITIONAL LEAN. Two MIXED that barely cleared the threshold.

That distribution is not random. Horror -- a genre that was once reliably neutral on politics, focused on universal fears like death, monsters, and the dark -- has been systematically colonized by progressive ideology over the past decade. The mechanism is simple: horror's tools (body violation, institutional betrayal, fear of the other) map too conveniently onto progressive frameworks (patriarchy as bodily violence, religion as institutional control, the marginalized as the feared other) for filmmakers to resist. The result is a genre that has become a delivery system for progressive messaging, often without audiences fully registering what they are absorbing.

A24 alone distributed four films on this list (Heretic, Midsommar, The Substance, MaXXXine). Their brand is built on art-house horror that systematically deconstructs traditional institutions. They are excellent filmmakers. They are also consistent in their targets. A24 treats Western Christian tradition, the nuclear family, and traditional gender roles as things to be dissected and consumed by horror. This is not a conspiracy. It is a business model.

Three patterns emerge clearly across these 20 films:

1. Religious institutions are the monster. Heretic, Immaculate, Leviticus, and The First Omen all position organized religion -- specifically Christianity and Catholicism -- as the source of horror. The Church is a conspiracy, a prison, an abuser. Faith is either naive or complicit. This is not an accident. It is a pattern.

2. The wealthy are literally evil. Ready or Not 2, Death of a Unicorn, They Will Kill You, and Clown in a Cornfield all frame wealthy people as demonic, murderous, or both. The eat-the-rich framework has become so common in horror that it is now the default setting for any film with a class dynamic.

3. Female rage is the hero. The Bride!, The Substance, MaXXXine, Lisa Frankenstein, and Immaculate all center women whose anger at patriarchal systems is the engine of the plot. These films are not about women overcoming obstacles. They are about women discovering that the obstacle is the system itself -- and then destroying it, often literally.

None of this means you should avoid horror. It means you should watch it with your eyes open. The scares are real. So is the messaging. And if you have teenagers, the messaging is reaching them whether you are in the room or not. Know what is on the screen before they press play.
